items.title: Indian Freedom and Indian Slavery in the Portuguese Amazon (1640–1755)
items.note: Examines the legal routes, such as ransoming and just war, by which Indigenous people were enslaved in the Portuguese Amazon, a region with no systematic count.

items.title: The Other Slavery: The Uncovered Story of Indian Enslavement in America
items.note: Offers the only hemispheric estimate, 2.5 to 5 million enslaved Indigenous people 1492–1900, aggregated from regional figures under a broad definition of slavery.

items.title: América en diásporas: esclavitudes y migraciones forzadas en Chile y otras regiones americanas (siglos XVI–XIX)
items.venue: RIL editores and Instituto de Historia, Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile
items.note: Collected studies of Indigenous and African forced migration in Chile and neighbouring regions, including the Mapuche captive trade.

items.title: Guest Editors' Introduction: New Directions in the History of Native American Slavery Studies
items.who: A. Bialuschewski and L. D. Fisher
items.note: Introduces a special issue surveying regional work on Native American slavery and the definitional problems that complicate any count.

items.title: Bancroft Prize awarded to The Other Slavery
items.note: The prize, following a National Book Award finalist listing, brought Reséndez's estimate into wide circulation as the standard figure.

items.title: The Other Slavery at the Heart of America: Andrés Reséndez, Indian Enslavement, and Looking South to Amazonia
items.venue: Middle Atlantic Review of Latin American Studies
items.note: Review essay testing Reséndez's framework against the Ecuadorian Amazon, one of the regions his estimate covers least.

items.title: Blacks of the Land: Indian Slavery, Settler Society, and the Portuguese Colonial Enterprise in South America
items.who: J. M. Monteiro (ed. and trans. J. Woodard and B. Weinstein)
items.note: English translation of Negros da terra, the core study of Indigenous slavery in São Paulo built on seventeenth-century probate inventories.

items.title: Indigenous Slavery from Out on the Edge
items.note: Argues that statistical anomalies and odd classifications in archives are central to assessing the scale of Indigenous slavery, not noise to be discarded.

items.title: Indigenous Slavery's Archive in Seventeenth-Century Chile
items.note: Analyses the military certificates that recorded the capture of Reche-Mapuche people, a document series that could support a Chilean count.

items.title: The Apache Diaspora: Four Centuries of Displacement and Survival
items.note: Traces Apache captives and deportees across northern New Spain, Mexico City and the Caribbean from the sixteenth to the nineteenth century.

items.title: Captives of Conquest: Slavery in the Early Modern Spanish Caribbean
items.note: Reconstructs the Indigenous slave trade into the Spanish Caribbean and argues that upwards of 250,000 people were enslaved there between the 1490s and 1542.

items.title: Mellon Foundation grant to Native Bound-Unbound: Archive of Indigenous Slavery
items.who: School for Advanced Research, Santa Fe (E. Rael-Gálvez)
items.note: A $1.5 million, three-year grant to digitize, transcribe and translate records of enslaved Indigenous people across the Americas into an open database.

items.title: In the Tethered Shadow: Native American Slavery, African Slavery, and the Disappearance of the Past
items.note: Considers how Native American slavery has receded from view beside African slavery in records and scholarship, which bears on assumptions about under-recording.

items.title: Aucaes desterrados a la ciudad: Esclavitud y resiliencia indígena en Santiago de Chile (siglo XVII)
items.venue: Revista Complutense de Historia de América
items.note: Follows Mapuche-Huilliche captives deported to Santiago, mostly women and children placed in domestic service and urban labour.

items.title: La esclavitud indígena en la América colonial: El contexto histórico general de la esclavitud mapuche durante el siglo XVII
items.note: Places the legalised enslavement of Mapuche people within the wider colonial system of Indigenous forced labour and servitude.

items.title: Stolen Relations public launch
items.who: Brown University (L. D. Fisher and tribal partners)
items.note: Tribally collaborative database opened to the public with about 7,000 records of individual enslaved Indigenous people, centred on New England.

items.title: Native Bound-Unbound: Archive of Indigenous Slavery goes live
items.who: School for Advanced Research, Santa Fe
items.note: Public site launched with records of 3,078 enslaved Indigenous people and 1,743 enslavers, linked to source documents, with about 1,000 more documents in process.
